input_references.role: Timestamped GPS trajectory points linked by trajectory_id
This file defines Montréal's island axis, which can be used as a baseline for route comparison.

metadata.goal: Analyze how returning-home travel differs from work and discretionary travel.
metadata.category: Multi-user work, discretionary, and returning-home trajectories with origin/destination land-use, transport mode, timing, island-axis direction, and point speeds. The accompanying montreal_island_axis.csv defines the analytical southwest–northeast baseline used for route comparison.
metadata.header: MTL Trajet: 16 Return Home Work Discretionary Patterns
metadata.dataset_description: Multi-user work, discretionary, and returning-home trajectories with origin/destination land-use, transport mode, timing, island-axis direction, and point speeds. The accompanying montreal_island_axis.csv defines the analytical southwest–northeast baseline used for route comparison.
metadata.metric_note: Distances are calculated from delivered GPS polylines; average point speed and duration are synchronized with the point table. Montréal's long island axis runs approximately southwest–northeast, so signed axis displacement summarizes the dominant travel direction.

plot.title: Departure Timing by Travel Purpose
plot.description: The plot is generated from the supplied case tables.

insight_list.question: How do departure times differ among work, returning-home, and discretionary trips?
insight_list.insight: Returning-home trips are strongly concentrated in the evening rush, while work trips peak earlier and discretionary trips remain more temporally dispersed.

plot.title: Opposite Work and Return-home Directions
plot.description: The plot is generated from the supplied case tables.

insight_list.question: How do signed island-axis displacements differ among work, return-home, café, and shopping trips?
insight_list.insight: Work and returning-home trajectories show opposite dominant directions along Montréal's island axis, unlike café and shopping trips, which are directionally dispersed.

plot.title: Home-bound Distance and Mode by Origin
plot.description: The plot is generated from the supplied case tables.

insight_list.question: How do home-bound distance and mode composition vary by origin land-use?
insight_list.insight: Home-bound trips from employment areas are longer and more mode-stable than those from shopping or café areas, which include more walking and cycling.

plot.title: Evening Home-destination Convergence
plot.description: The plot is generated from the supplied case tables.

insight_list.question: Does the number of home destination zones decline from early to late evening within each origin land-use?
insight_list.insight: Home-bound trajectories from similar origin land-use increasingly converge toward a smaller set of residential or mixed destination areas as evening progresses.

insights: Returning-home trips are strongly concentrated in the evening rush, while work trips peak earlier and discretionary trips remain more temporally dispersed.
Work and returning-home trajectories show opposite dominant directions along Montréal's island axis, unlike café and shopping trips, which are directionally dispersed.
Home-bound trips from employment areas are longer and more mode-stable than those from shopping or café areas, which include more walking and cycling.
Home-bound trajectories from similar origin land-use increasingly converge toward a smaller set of residential or mixed destination areas as evening progresses.
summary: Returning-home travel is evening-concentrated and generally opposes morning work movement along Montréal's island axis. Employment-origin home trips are longer and more consistently motorized, while later home-bound trips converge on fewer destination areas.
evidence_policy: Claims describe patterns in this controlled constructed dataset and do not establish causal relationships.
